channel.title: Issam Sayyaf — Blog
channel.description: Notes on time-series deep learning, embedded ML, firmware and signal processing.

item.title: TimesNet, explained from scratch
item.description: A time series is the wrong shape. TimesNet folds it into a grid on the period an FFT finds, so a 3x3 convolution can see both kinds of neighbour a time point has. Built up one step at a time on twelve numbers you can check by hand, with an animation per step — and two findings about the code that the paper does not mention.

item.title: DLinear, explained from scratch
item.description: One linear layer beat every published Transformer at long-horizon forecasting. This is how it works, step by step through a forward pass — every matrix built by hand on a worked example, twelve animations, and a look inside the 32,256 weights at what it actually learned.

item.title: PatchTST, explained from scratch
item.description: A one-layer linear model was beating every Transformer at long-term forecasting. PatchTST shows the Transformer was never the problem — the tokenization was. Two changes, patching and channel-independence, every equation worked through, with animations and figures computed from a real forward pass.

item.title: TS2Vec, explained from scratch
item.description: How TS2Vec learns one vector per timestamp with no labels at all — two overlapping crops, a mask, a dilated CNN, and a hierarchical contrastive loss. With every equation, worked numbers, and animations for the parts that need motion.

item.title: How this blog works
item.description: Every post is one Markdown file in _posts/. This one doubles as a formatting reference — delete it once you have written your own.
